title: Fearchar sits two nights over Leabhar Baile thais
summary: A copy of the grievance book reaches Muileann dhearg folded in a meal-sack, and Fearchar Bàrd, a breaker of coal at the belt since boyhood, reads it by tallow light two nights running. He finds he can put nothing of his own into its columns, though he knows the granary's short week and the stream at Doire mhòr as well as any hand that wrote there.

title: Griogair mac Aonghais tells Fearchar to sing it
summary: Old Griogair mac Aonghais, who broke coal beside Fearchar's father before him, tells Fearchar that a column is for men who have given up hoping to be heard, and that he should sing the grievance instead of writing it. Fearchar carries the book back to Baile thais and begins working verses to the granary's short week.

title: Fearchar's first song sung at the pit-mouth
summary: Fearchar Bàrd sings his first finished song, four verses on the Levy and the famine, at the pit-mouth of Muileann dhearg while the crews wait out a stopped winding-gear. It is carried to Baile thais within the month by crews he never asked to carry it.

title: The overseer's clerk copies the forbidden song
summary: An overseer at Baile thais has Fearchar's song taken down word for word from a boy of the crews so that it can be shown forbidden, and a docker's pay is cut by half a week for the singing of it. The clerk's copy, made to condemn the song, becomes the only complete written record of it.

title: Fearchar repays the docked wage
summary: Fearchar Bàrd walks to Baile thais to repay out of his own wage the boy docked half a week's pay for singing his song, and the boy refuses the coin, saying he would rather have sung it than not. The song is sung again within the week, further than before.

title: The song reaches An Taigh-òsta Grianach
summary: Carters carry Fearchar Bàrd's song east along the road before he ever travels it himself, and it is taken up by the custom of An Taigh-òsta Grianach, whose keeper asks no questions of a tune that pleases her house. The Company's own carters learn it there without knowing whose grievance they sing.

title: Fearchar hears his own song sung unknowing
summary: Riding east on the silver guild's business, Fearchar Bàrd sits unknown at An Taigh-òsta Grianach and hears six Company carters sing his granary song through, missing a line they cannot remember. He says nothing of whose it is, and finds the mis-singing harder to bear than the forbidding had been.

title: The fire-ship loads at Ros dhomhain
summary: Fearchar Bàrd, at Ros dhomhain on the silver guild's errand, watches the Company's first iron steamship take on coal through the night at the new deep-water quay, burning the island's own fuel to carry the rest away. He stands at the rail until past midnight, watching the loading by lamplight.

title: Fearchar makes the ship song
summary: That same night, sitting on the new quay's coiled rope, Fearchar Bàrd makes the song of the ship that eats the hill to carry the hill away, the most quoted of all his songs. He sings it first to the loading gang he stood beside, too tired themselves to do more than nod.

title: The wall rises at Baile thais
summary: The Company rings the pithead at Baile thais with a stone wall and a single gate through the summer, and sets a lamed former hewer to keep the tally-book at the gate. Fearchar Bàrd, home from Ros dhomhain, walks the wall's length and makes no song of it that year.

title: Catrìona nic Eachainn buried at Muileann chiar
summary: A dozen of Baile thais who remembered the eleven days walk twenty miles east to bury Catrìona nic Eachainn, a refiner of the silver guild to her last day, and the Company docks each of them a day's pay for the going. Fearchar Bàrd, too young to have known her striking, walks with them.

title: Fearchar makes Catrìona's lament
summary: On the walk home from Muileann chiar, Fearchar Bàrd makes the lament for Catrìona nic Eachainn, naming the coal-tub and the empty shelves she counted and the guild's bench where she stood to the end, and ending it, as her life had ended, without complaint. The dozen who had known her weep at it on the road.

title: The quay sheds burn three days at Ros dhomhain
summary: A fire in the Company's coal sheds at Ros dhomhain burns three days and takes two streets of the harbour quarter, and the telling grows three causes before the Company's own inquiry finds none at all. News of it reaches Baile thais and Muileann dhearg by rider within the week.

title: The carters sing the ship song for their own quay
summary: At An Taigh-òsta Grianach, Fearchar Bàrd hears the fire-ship's carters sing his ship song louder and rougher than before, now that their own quay has burned, though none of them know the song or its maker. He sits again unknown, and does not tell them.

title: Artair mac Iain dies at Cathair dhearg
summary: Artair mac Iain, high custodian for twenty and four years, dies at Cathair dhearg at eighty years old. Word of his death reaches Fearchar Bàrd on the road home from An Taigh-òsta Grianach, carried faster than either fire or song by a rider changing horses at every post-house.

title: The Council of Custodians rises without a name
summary: Called to choose Artair mac Iain's successor, the Council of Custodians sits three days at Cathair dhearg and rises without agreeing one, and the high custodian's chair stands empty at the table's head through the Faoilleach that follows. It is said that Robert Haskins at the Residency finds an empty seat easier to deal with than a full one.
